How is this not a feature yet?  I get the immersion argument, but the reality is that most people aren't using VR headsets in VRC.  Even those who have VR headsets will use it without them because sometimes they want to socialize in VRC without having to dedicate themselves 100% to being in VR.

Having to remove a headset to do anything outside of VR can be annoying, especially if you want to multitask a little.  And having to get on your mic, or put on a regular headset, just to casually connect to VRC is silly when basic text chat support would be more convenient.  That VRC seems to have issues swapping audio sources while it's running, meaning I have to restart it just to swap between speakers and headset, isn't helping.

That's before getting into the fact that not everyone wants to use voice.  It's a comfort issue, and forcing anyone who wants to socialize at all to do it in a way they're uncomfortable with is a bit weird.  Sure there are tools for writing in the air, but unless they have and are using a VR headset they won't have the hand tracking to make that effective.  Writing in the air with the mouse is a pretty sloppy option (and seems only marginally more immersive than text chat, as far as communicating goes).

While I have many issues with VRC, this one discourages me from using it the most because I can't simply log on and chat, I have to either be mute (and maybe message through Discord or Steam) or I have to suit up.

Immersion is great, but so is flexibility.  If a user wants to block all text chat, make that an option.  They'll be ignoring everyone who tries to communicate that way, arguably to everyone's detriment, which is effectively what's being forced on everyone now for no good reason.  At least this would make it an option.

Woah, I get to close a request from before I played VRChat.
Anyways, we have a text chatbox now that you can use. Open your Action Menu, go to Options, then go to Chatbox. (Easier access pending)
You can send chat messages, and people can see the messages appear over your head. The visibility of these messages is meant to emulate voice reach (so if you can't hear someone, you can't see the messages either)
The messages are not logged and are ephemeral. Once they're gone, they're gone.
We're still improving this system, but let's go ahead and close this.
